facts.heading: The human part still matters.
facts.body: As AI reshapes work, employers are paying renewed attention to communication, critical thinking, creativity, empathy, and other human strengths—and English and the humanities are part of that conversation.

facts.heading: English stands out at UNO.
facts.body: In 2024, English was among UNO’s five most specialized fields by degree concentration compared with the national pattern.

facts.heading: When everyone has access to the same AI tools, what sets your work apart?
facts.body: Voice. Judgment. Context. Creativity. Understanding people. Communicating something worth remembering. Those are some of the human qualities bringing English and the humanities into new conversations about work in the AI era.

facts.heading: English doesn’t lead to just one kind of work.
facts.body: English graduates in the UK move into education, marketing and PR, administration, arts and media, writing and translation, and many other fields. The common thread isn’t one job title. It’s what you can do with language, ideas, evidence, and people.
facts.source: HESA Graduate Outcomes data, reported by Prospects, 2024
